name: Breathing
desc: Breathe in and out. Watch the ribs, intercostal muscles and diaphragm move, and see why air flows in.
subject: biology

name: Gas Exchange
desc: Watch oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse in an alveolus. Change the wall, blood flow and breathing.
subject: biology

name: Microscope
desc: Place an onion slide, choose a lens and focus with the coarse and fine knobs. Work out the magnification.
subject: biology

name: Joints
desc: Bend hinge joints, swing ball-and-socket joints, take away the cartilage and fluid, and find what ligaments and tendons join.
subject: biology

name: Muscle Pairs
desc: Bend the arm and the knee. See which muscle contracts and which relaxes.
subject: biology

name: Digestive System
desc: Follow a meal from mouth to anus. Tap each organ, then test which enzyme breaks down each food.
subject: biology

name: Pondweed
desc: Move the lamp and count the oxygen bubbles. Find the mean and plot how light affects photosynthesis.
subject: biology

name: Flower Parts
desc: Label a flower, dissect a lily, pollinate with a bee or the wind, grow a pollen tube and find what seeds need to germinate.
subject: biology

name: Food Web
desc: Draw the arrows, find the food chains, then remove an animal and see what happens to the rest of the web.
subject: biology

name: Natural Selection
desc: Turn the bark sooty, let the birds hunt and the moths breed, and watch the peppered moth population change over generations.
subject: biology

name: Molecule Builder
desc: Join atoms to build water, carbon dioxide and methane. Sort elements, compounds and mixtures, and read chemical formulae.
subject: chemistry

name: Periodic Table Explorer
desc: Find the metals and non-metals, test samples, spot trends down groups and across periods, and see how the table was built.
subject: chemistry

name: Balance the Equation
desc: Change the big numbers until every atom is equal on both sides. Three levels, hints and your own equations.
subject: chemistry

name: Particle Model
desc: Heat and cool a substance. Watch the particles melt, boil, condense and freeze.
subject: chemistry

name: Diffusion
desc: Lift the barrier and race hot against cold. Watch gases and dye spread out.
subject: chemistry

name: Gas Pressure
desc: Pump in particles, heat them or squash them. Watch the pressure gauge.
subject: chemistry

name: Indicator Lab
desc: Test solutions with litmus, red cabbage and universal indicator. Find acid, neutral or alkali, and the pH.
subject: chemistry

name: Neutralise It
desc: Add alkali to acid drop by drop. Watch the colour and pH reach 7, then overshoot. Match stings and cures.
subject: chemistry

name: Acid Strength
desc: Choose a strong or weak acid and how concentrated it is. Watch the particles split up and see the pH.
subject: chemistry

name: Naming Salts
desc: Mix an acid with a metal, a base or a carbonate. Watch what happens, then build the salt's name.
subject: chemistry

name: Dissolving
desc: Add sugar, salt or sand to water or oil. Watch the balance and the particles, and find when it is saturated.
subject: chemistry

name: Separate It
desc: Filter, evaporate, distil and run chromatography. Get the salt out of rock salt.
subject: chemistry

name: Metal Reactions
desc: Heat metals in a flame, drop them in water or steam, then build the reactivity series from your evidence.
subject: chemistry

name: Displacement Lab
desc: Put a metal in a solution. Does it push the other metal out? Use the reactivity series to predict.
subject: chemistry

name: Spring Stretch
desc: Hang masses on a spring, measure the extension and plot the graph. Find the elastic limit, and see why the floor pushes back.
subject: physics

name: Balanced Forces
desc: Run a tug of war, drive a rocket car with a parachute, and decide which forces are balanced in the forces circus.
subject: physics

name: Moon Phases
desc: Move the Moon round the Earth and see its phase from the UK. Compare the old and new models of the Universe.
subject: physics

name: Make a Wave
desc: Shake a slinky up and down or push and pull it. Follow the red coil, label the wave and see two waves meet.
subject: physics

name: Sound Waves
desc: Change loudness and pitch. Watch the air particles and the oscilloscope trace.
subject: physics

name: Echo Timer
desc: Clap, time the echo and work out how far away the cliff, seabed or moth is.
subject: physics

name: Light Rays
desc: Aim a ray box at a mirror or glass block. Measure angles from the normal.
subject: physics

name: Colour Mixer
desc: Mix coloured lights, use filters and light up objects. Predict what you will see.
subject: physics

name: Lens and Eye
desc: Focus an image with a convex lens, then label the eye and compare it with a camera.
subject: physics

name: Static Charge
desc: Rub a balloon on a jumper and count the electrons that move. Then see how charged balloons push and pull.
subject: physics

name: Circuit Builder
desc: Build series and parallel circuits. Add cells and bulbs, then read the ammeters and voltmeters.
subject: physics

name: Electromagnet
desc: Change the turns, current and core. Count the paper clips and record a fair test.
subject: physics

name: Skate Ramp
desc: Let a skater roll down a ramp. Watch the energy move between the stores, then switch friction on and see where it goes.
subject: physics

name: Heat Flow
desc: Touch a hot block to a cool one and watch them reach the same temperature. Compare a pool and a cup, then metal and wood.
subject: physics

name: Graph It
desc: Fill in a results table, find the mean and the anomaly, plot the graph and draw a line of best fit.
subject: ws

name: DNA Builder
desc: Build nucleotides, join them by condensation, then pair antiparallel strands into a double helix.
subject: biology
topic: OCR A 2.1.3 Nucleotides and nucleic acids

name: DNA Replication
desc: Copy DNA at a replication fork with gyrase, helicase, DNA polymerase and ligase, then test the three models with Meselson and Stahl.
subject: biology
topic: OCR A 2.1.3 Nucleotides and nucleic acids

name: Action Potential
desc: Stimulate an axon membrane, watch the Na⁺ and K⁺ channels and the trace, then race myelinated and unmyelinated axons.
subject: biology

name: Protein Synthesis
desc: Transcribe a gene into mRNA in the nucleus, then translate it codon by codon at a ribosome. Explore the genetic code and mutations.
subject: biology
topic: OCR A 2.1.3 Nucleotides and nucleic acids

name: Reaction Lab
desc: Spot the signs of a reaction, burn fuels and test the products, compare fuels, heat carbonates and sort exothermic from endothermic. Then build the word equations.
subject: chemistry

name: Seesaw
desc: Balance a seesaw, turn a nut with a spanner and lift a load with a lever. Work out each moment and predict which way it tips.
subject: physics

name: Motion Graphs
desc: Work out speeds, time a trolley down a ramp, then drive a walker and watch the distance–time graph draw itself. Match a graph and read the speed from it.
subject: physics

name: Pressure Lab
desc: Sink blocks and people into sand and mud to see how area changes pressure. Then lower a sensor into water, pull the tape off a bottle of jets and explore upthrust.
subject: physics

name: Food Tests Lab
desc: Test foods with iodine, Benedict's, biuret and ethanol, then work out what is in mystery samples and watch an enzyme digest starch.
subject: biology

name: Cell Builder
desc: Build animal and plant cells part by part, compare them on a Venn diagram, and explore how specialised cells are adapted to their jobs.
subject: biology

name: Mass and Weight
desc: Weigh objects on a newtonmeter and a balance on Earth, the Moon and beyond, and use weight = mass × g.
subject: physics

name: Variation Sorter
desc: Sort characteristics by cause and type, then measure a made-up class and choose a bar chart or histogram.
subject: biology

name: Seasons
desc: Move the Earth round the Sun and spin it to see how the tilted axis causes day length, Sun height and the seasons.
subject: physics

name: Menstrual Cycle
desc: Step through the 28-day cycle on a dial, watch the uterus lining and the egg, see what changes if the egg is fertilised, and sort condoms and the pill.
subject: biology

name: Extracting Metals
desc: Use the reactivity series to choose how a metal is extracted, heat metal oxides with carbon, and work out how much metal an ore holds.
subject: chemistry

name: Solar System Scale
desc: Put the planets in order, walk out the Solar System to scale with Earth at 1 m, explore the planet data and see how a day on Venus is longer than its year.
subject: physics
